name: GLS
summary: Android test automation and build optimisation for logistics and field operations, with substantial reductions in build times.
context: A multi-app Android environment supporting logistics and field operations. The contribution covered automated testing, build optimisation, engineering processes and knowledge sharing.
work: Supported automated testing across the Android app environment.
Optimised builds alongside the test automation work to shorten feedback times for the team.
Contributed improvements to engineering processes.
Shared testing and delivery knowledge with the team.
outcome: Substantially reduced build times alongside improvements to automated testing, giving the team faster feedback on changes.

name: Zuriga
summary: A connected coffee machine app, rebuilt across Android and iOS.
context: An existing Kotlin Multiplatform app connected users to their coffee machine. The brief was to take over the app, replace its interface, and improve the business logic around Bluetooth Low Energy communication.
work: Took over the existing codebase, working largely independently with support from the design team.
Rebuilt the complete user interface across Android and iOS using Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform.
Improved the BLE-related business logic used to communicate with the connected machine.
outcome: A fully rewritten interface with a simpler, more modern product feel across Android and iOS, alongside improvements to the machine-communication logic.

name: Siresca
summary: Android development for an app supporting electrical installation work on site.
context: Siresca overlays installation plans on the real construction site using augmented reality and supports documentation, progress tracking and task capture. James contributed to the existing Android app through Milk Interactive.
work: Developed features for the Android application.
Fixed bugs in the existing codebase.

name: Fresenius Medical Care
summary: Dialysis UI applications built for a custom Android device.
context: A custom AOSP-based device connected to a dialysis device needed a new set of applications. The user-facing interface had to present information from the clinic and device and guide users through device-related steps and status.
work: Held responsibility for three applications: the user-facing UI and supporting service apps.
Built the apps from scratch in collaboration with the design team.
Integrated accessibility, security, automated testing, and internationalization into the implementation.
outcome: Three purpose-built Android applications, covering the user interface and supporting services, with accessibility and internationalization incorporated from the start. The work provides concrete experience of building Android software for a specialised healthcare device.

name: blackned
summary: Android platform engineering with faster build and delivery workflows.
context: An AOSP-based communication platform in a high-security environment needed senior Android engineering support. Alongside product development, build and CI/CD workflows were a focus for improvement.
work: Worked with the team as a senior Android developer on the communication platform.
Improved Gradle build workflows.
Improved the CI/CD pipeline while working within the constraints of a high-security engineering environment.
outcome: Reduced Gradle build times by around 50% and total CI/CD pipeline time by around 60% in this project’s development environment, shortening the wait for build and pipeline feedback.

name: lexoffice
summary: Strengthening Android UI testing and its infrastructure.
context: James worked on lexoffice first as a freelance Android developer and later as a full-time senior Android developer. His contributions spanned UI testing and its infrastructure, feature development and engineering improvements across the Android app environment.
work: Applied Android UI testing expertise to the application.
Worked on the supporting test infrastructure.
Helped the team increase automated test coverage.
Delivered features and bug fixes during the later full-time role.

name: EsperoTech / wearit4U
summary: Android feature development and bug fixes for an orthopedic wear-time app.
context: Through EsperoTech, James contributed to the wearit4U Android app, a product for documenting the actual wear time of orthopedic aids.
work: Developed new features for the Android app.
Fixed bugs in the existing application.

name: Neurofly
summary: Android development guidance and architecture support.
context: Collaboration on the Neurofly Android project, with a focus on further development, code review and architectural recommendations.
work: Reviewed code and shared development practices.
Provided architecture recommendations for the application.
Supported the project owner and team with Android engineering guidance.

name: LTE Consulting / Marktmeister Pro
summary: Development across around five apps, including Marktgalerie and Markttagmeister.
context: A collaboration with LTE Consulting covering around five applications. The work included Marktgalerie for event photo documentation, Markttagmeister for on-site event organisation, and SeeQRe for scanning and decoding QR codes. Marktgalerie began with a prototype audit and consulting before expanding into further development.
work: Contributed Android development, architecture, app design and feature implementation across the app portfolio.
Reviewed the Marktgalerie prototype and took on further development of its photo documentation features.
Worked on apps supporting event organisation and QR-code scanning.

name: J&C Bachmann
summary: Modernizing an established Android app and its surrounding platform.
context: A long-running collaboration across an Android app, Node.js backend and Vue.js web portal. The existing Java codebase needed continued development and a gradual move to Kotlin.
work: Modernized and extended the Java application while migrating it to Kotlin.
Worked across the mobile app and surrounding web and backend stack.
Supported delivery through ongoing collaboration and technical guidance.

name: Benefits.me
summary: Senior Android support inside an existing mobile team.
context: Support and guidance for the Benefits.me mobile team, combining Android development expertise with quality management and clear technical feedback.
work: Supported the team’s Android development work.
Provided practical code and engineering feedback.
Contributed guidance on programming and quality management.

name: farmerJoe
summary: Engineering support across the stack and the delivery process.
context: As a full-time software engineer at farmerJoe, James worked across mobile apps, the React web application and a Firebase backend for a platform connecting farmers and food-industry businesses.
work: Worked across the stack to solve product engineering problems.
Helped improve development processes.
Supported the quality and efficiency of team collaboration.

name: Hansgrohe Group
summary: Connected product apps for homeowners and professional installers.
context: As a full-time mobile application developer at Hansgrohe Group, James worked on hansgrohe home and hansgrohe SmartExpert. The products connected homeowners and trained installers with digital water and shower systems. His core focus was Android, with contributions across iOS and backend integration.
work: Developed Android applications using Kotlin and MVVM, including leading Android delivery for SmartExpert.
Integrated apps with connected devices, backend APIs and third-party services.
Implemented automated UI and unit tests and contributed code reviews and technical documentation.

name: StarJar
summary: Everyday chores become stars, routines and family rewards.
context: StarJar gives parents a way to create tasks and choose rewards, while children earn stars for completed chores. Read-aloud support helps children who are not yet reading independently.
work: Task templates, schedules, reminders, badges and streak bonuses.
Multiple child profiles with parent approval and PIN-protected settings.
Read-aloud tasks and rewards, with an interface designed for children and parents.

name: Don’t Go To Bed
summary: A family adventure made with my sons, Leo and Ian.
context: Explore, build and find Mammy before nightfall. The game grew out of the boys’ ideas, with playable family characters and a new world each session. Available on Android, iPhone and iPad.
work: Break and collect blocks to build a route through the world.
Explore from different directions and play together on a trusted local Wi-Fi network.
Free gameplay, no ads and no game account; optional support tips sit behind a grown-ups gate.

name: Android Security Training
summary: Practical labs that connect Android vulnerabilities to working fixes.
context: Hands-on training for Android developers and mobile teams. Vulnerable and secure application variants make it possible to inspect a weakness, understand its cause, apply a fix and retest.
work: Network trust and payload encryption, including HTTPS and certificate pinning.
Reverse engineering and APK tampering, runtime permissions and IPC.
WebView and local data risks, with practical verification in the training labs.

name: Elchem
summary: A real-world map becomes a place for encounters and discovery.
context: Elchem combines exploration with a game world of elements, recipes, equipment and encounters. Players choose a route and discover what awaits at the next map point.
work: Map-based exploration with encounters and places to prepare.
Elements, recipes and equipment woven into the game experience.
An Android product with gameplay previews and a Google Play listing.

name: Watchful
summary: Keep track of the things you want to check, without the mental list.
context: Watchful brings personal watchlists to a phone: from looking for a better price nearby to keeping an eye out for a favourite show. The product page explains the experience, plans and support options. Available on Android, iPhone and iPad.
work: Create a watchlist around the things that matter to you.
A free starting tier with additional capacity through Pro.
Dedicated support, privacy information and data deletion guidance.

name: WiFiWizard
summary: An open-source example of Wi-Fi connections and QR scanning on Android.
context: A practical Android example combining programmatic Wi-Fi connections with QR code scanning. It provides source code for teams exploring device connectivity in a Compose app.
work: Programmatic Wi-Fi connections with error handling and fallback behaviour.
ML Kit QR scanning and AdMob integration.
Jetpack Compose UI with an example Espresso test.

name: TrustKeyService
summary: A proof of concept for keystore-backed operations on a custom Android device.
context: An Android Keystore experiment exposing cryptographic operations through a Binder service. It documents a hardware-backed TEE result on a specific device, alongside the limits of what the experiment establishes.
work: Generate and inspect an AES key in Android Keystore.
Expose generate, inspect, encrypt, decrypt, and delete operations through AIDL.
Exercise a debug-only test path from a host machine through adb.

name: Bluetooth File Transfer
summary: A BLE file-transfer proof of concept between Android and a laptop.
context: The Android phone acts as a BLE peripheral with a GATT file-transfer service. A Python client on a laptop can exchange files with selected Android folders.
work: Upload and download files or folders over BLE.
Keep advertising and transfer state in an Android foreground service.
Use a Compose interface for permissions, folder selection, and transfer state.

name: Example Wear App
summary: A phone-and-watch sample demonstrating control handoff and state synchronisation.
context: A paired Android and Wear OS sample coordinating control state and profiles through the Wear Data Layer, including fallback behaviour when devices cannot communicate.
work: Coordinate the active controller between phone and watch.
Synchronise profiles using Data Items.
Demonstrate connection awareness and a local emergency takeover.

name: The Muse Agency
summary: A website showcasing the people and creative services behind The Muse Agency.
context: The Muse Agency brings together talent and content creation in Dublin. Its website introduces the agency, its roster of creators and its content services.
work: Built the agency website with sections for talent and content creation.
Created a route from browsing the agency’s work to making an enquiry.

name: Atelier Wiessalla
summary: A website introducing Inga Wiessalla’s creative workshop in Düsseldorf.
context: Atelier Wiessalla offers individual creative sessions and family activities using origami, drawing and other techniques. The website introduces Inga, her approach and the ways visitors can work with her.
work: Built a website presenting the workshop, its activities and the artist’s background.
Included contact information and legal pages alongside the workshop content.

name: Einzigartiganderssein
summary: WordPress website changes and ongoing support for Einzigartiganderssein, a Swiss client, by freelance developer James Cullimore.
context: Work on an existing WordPress website, making changes to support the client’s business.
work: Made changes to the client’s WordPress website.
Supported website updates as part of the client engagement.

summary: Business-process and email automation, Webflow updates and technical advice for Horoskop-Paradies, with support for wider business decisions.
context: The engagement extended beyond website development into the day-to-day technical and business decisions behind Horoskop-Paradies. I acted as a technical lead and adviser, taking on responsibilities comparable to a CTO alongside hands-on implementation.

Worked on Webflow updates, APIs and webhooks.
Researched astrology APIs and automation options to inform implementation decisions.
Helped make decisions about analytics, Google Ads and social media.
Searched for bloggers and marketing support to help the business.
Worked directly with the client on technical priorities and wider business decisions.
